title: Inter-region bootstrap synchronization, bandwidth-constrained upgrades, and deterministic rollback criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: customers operating Private/VPC deployments across multiple regions (or multi-site corporate datacenters) need a predictable, auditable upgrade and bootstrap process that works under constrained cross-site bandwidth and in air-gapped environments. Current upgrade flows assume ample inter-region bandwidth and simple mirroring, which causes long upgrade windows, missed SLAs, and opaque rollback behavior when syncs fail. This ticket defines requirements and acceptance criteria for: 1) deterministic inter-region bootstrap synchronization under bandwidth caps; 2) staged upgrade orchestration that can shed non-critical traffic and prioritize control-plane/critical data; and 3) explicit, deterministic rollback triggers and automated operator playbooks suitable for air-gapped and bandwidth-constrained customers.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A documented inter-region bootstrap plan exists that lists required artifacts, priorities (control-plane, runtime images, operator manifests, signature files), and maximum per-site bandwidth ceilings configurable by customer.

AC-2: Upgrade orchestration supports a 'bandwidth-shed' mode that automatically sequences artifact transfer in priority order and enforces a configurable bytes-per-minute cap per peering link without human intervention.

AC-3: Deterministic rollback conditions are defined and implemented: artifact checksum mismatch, KMS key rotation failure, >15% node loss in a single site for >5 minutes, or failed canary health checks for 3 consecutive probe windows trigger an automated rollback or operator alert depending on policy.

AC-4: Air-gapped customer acceptance: the bootstrap plan includes an offline artifact bundle format and validation steps; a dry-run local validation command verifies artifact integrity and operator actions without egress and returns a pass/fail exit code.

AC-5: Upgrade window SLOs: for N-site deployment where inter-site link is <100 Mbps, the orchestration can complete control-plane upgrade within defined time budget (configurable; default 45 minutes) while leaving data-plane serving degraded no more than 10% CPU latency increase for majority of workloads.

AC-6: Telemetry and audit: every artifact transfer, signature verification, and rollback decision is emitted to the customer's audit log and to the Redwood Console (or local collector) with minimal schema that includes timestamps, checksums, bytes transferred, and decision reason.

AC-7: Operator runbook exists with play-by-play steps for manual intervention, and it has been validated in at least two internal QA runs with simulated bandwidth constraints and one air-gapped dry run.
AC-8: Backwards compatibility: existing private deploy customers who do not opt into bandwidth-shed mode see no change in default behavior unless explicit configuration is applied.
AC-9: Automated tests: e2e upgrade test harness includes a throttled-network scenario and an air-gapped file-install path; these tests are green in CI on the release branch.
AC-10: Customer-facing docs and checklist published in Confluence and linked from Console within release notes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spec+design): final review with Security and Migrations — 2 weeks
Phase 1 (control-plane only canary): enable bandwidth-shed for control-plane artifacts between two non-production sites with telemetry collection enabled — 1 week
Phase 2 (canary runtime): run staged runtime upgrade with 10% of customer capacity in downgraded bandwidth link and validate rollback triggers — 2 weeks
Phase 3 (pilot customers): onboard 2-3 pilot customers with varying network characteristics (air-gapped, low-bandwidth inter-site, normal) — 3 weeks
Phase 4 (GA): enable feature as opt-in and publish docs, run post-deploy audit for first 24h for pilot customers — 1 week
upgrade_playbook: Step 0: Preflight checks — connectivity matrix, available disk, k8s operator version, KMS key accessibility (or offline key presence).
Step 1: Generate signed artifact bundle with manifest and prioritized object list for targeted sites.
Step 2: Initiate control-plane update on leader site and enable bandwidth-shed limits for peer replication links.
Step 3: Perform canary health checks (liveness, readiness, KV cache warmup) for 15m; if any check fails 3x mark canary failed and trigger rollback.
Step 4: Stage runtime images to remaining sites in priority order (control plane, operator, runtime-critical libs, optional assets).
Step 5: Validate signatures and checksums on arrival; if mismatch, mark artifact invalid and abort staged propagation, notify operator with remediation steps.
Step 6: Promote staged site once health checks pass and aggregate latency/cost metrics are within thresholds.
Step 7: Post-upgrade scrub: validate model-serving correctness with smoke evals and run token-rate performance test for 10m.
Step 8: If rollback decision is made, perform deterministic reverse-order rollback using signed rollback manifests and log every action to audit stream.
test_plan: Network-throttle e2e: simulate 50 Mbps and 10 Mbps inter-site links; measure completion time and correctness of artifact application.
Air-gap dry-run: produce offline artifact bundle, transfer via simulated physical media, perform local validation without egress.
Chaos: induce node drain and simultaneous artifact mismatch to validate rollback policy and observability.
Performance-safety: measure tail latency for inference while upgrade runs in bandwidth-shed mode; must remain within 10% of baseline 95th percentile latency.
Audit validation: check that every upgrade step produces audit events with required fields and that events can be ingested by customer SIEM.
notes: Trade-off: aggressive parallel replication reduces total upgrade time but increases risk of cascading failures if checksums diverge; bandwidth-shed mode chooses safety by default.

Open question: should rollback be automatic for checksum mismatch in air-gapped sites where operator cannot fetch replacement artifact? Proposal: abort and require operator manual approval for irreversible actions.
Operational consideration: include a 'simulated' dry-run option in Console that shows transfer plan and estimated time under current caps without performing writes.
UX: provide clear customer-facing UI to set per-link caps and artifact priorities; defaults should be conservative for non-expert operators.
